sentences.en: Over the past three decades, ADHD diagnoses in the United States have been climbing steadily and so have prescriptions for the medication to manage the symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 在过去三十年里，美国的ADHD（注意缺陷多动障碍）诊断率一直在稳步攀升，用于控制症状的药物处方量也随之增加。

sentences.en: But as the field booms, some long-time researchers are starting to question whether much of the fundamental thinking around how we identify and treat the disorder is wrong.
sentences.zh: 但随着该领域的发展，一些资深研究人员开始质疑，我们识别和治疗该疾病的基本思路是否在很大程度上是错误的。

sentences.en: Today, magazine contributor Paul Tuff explains.
sentences.zh: 今天，杂志撰稿人保罗·塔夫将对此进行解读。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, June 17th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月17日，星期二。

sentences.en: Paul, welcome back to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 保罗，欢迎回到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Paul, you recently wrote a story about ADHD that got a lot of people's attention, including here on The Daily.
sentences.zh: 保罗，你最近写了一篇关于ADHD的报道，引起了很多人的关注，包括我们《每日新闻》的听众。

sentences.en: And it might be because ADHD and the medications to treat it are something that, frankly, I think a lot of people seem to have kind of a personal experience with,
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为ADHD及其治疗药物，坦白说，我认为很多人似乎都有过某种亲身经历，

sentences.en: either themselves or people that they know.
sentences.zh: 要么是他们自己，要么是他们认识的人。

sentences.en: And so my first question to you is just how did you personally come to this story?
sentences.zh: 所以我问你的第一个问题是，你是如何亲自接触到这个故事的？

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's a lot like what you're describing.
sentences.zh: 是的，这和你描述的情况很像。

sentences.en: I have two boys, one who's 10 and one who's 15.
sentences.zh: 我有两个儿子，一个10岁，一个15岁。

sentences.en: So they are both in the key ADHD demographic.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都处于ADHD的关键人口统计学范围内。

sentences.en: And I think a few years ago, I just started to have this sense that, like, ADHD was all around me, that every conversation I was having with parents and with teachers,
sentences.zh: 我想几年前，我开始有种感觉，ADHD似乎无处不在，我和家长及老师的每一次谈话，

sentences.en: that this was a big part of what they were concerned with and what they were trying to figure out.
sentences.zh: 这都是他们关心和试图弄清楚的重要部分。

sentences.en: But it felt like there were a lot of puzzles in this diagnosis, that on the one hand, it seemed like something that was very clear and straightforward.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这个诊断中有很多谜团，一方面，它看起来似乎非常清晰明了。

sentences.en: Like a friend would say, yeah, we didn't know what was wrong, but then we found out it's ADHD.
sentences.zh: 比如朋友会说，是的，我们以前不知道出了什么问题，但后来发现是ADHD。

sentences.en: But at the same time, it felt like the boundaries between what was ADHD and what was not ADHD were kind of fluid and porous.
sentences.zh: 但同时，ADHD与非ADHD之间的界限似乎又有些模糊和多孔。

sentences.en: And so I wanted to try to understand this disconnect.
sentences.zh: 所以我想要理解这种脱节。

sentences.en: And I figured the place to start was to talk to the scientists who study ADHD.
sentences.zh: 我想起点应该是去采访那些研究ADHD的科学家们。

sentences.en: So when you started diving into this field that it sounds like seemed both everywhere, but also a little bit hard to pin down, what did you find?
sentences.zh: 当你开始深入研究这个领域时，听起来它似乎既无处不在，又有点难以捉摸，你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Like, what did these researchers tell you about the landscape of our understanding of this condition?
sentences.zh: 这些研究人员对我们理解这种疾病的现状说了些什么？

sentences.en: Well, I found that they were a little confused as well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我发现他们自己也感到有些困惑。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Hey, is that Edmund?
sentences.zh: 嘿，那是埃德蒙吗？

sentences.en: It's Edmund, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是埃德蒙，没错。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: One whose work and whose thinking I found most interesting was this British researcher named Edmund Sanuga Bark.
sentences.zh: 我发现其中一位工作和思想最有趣的研究人员，是一位名叫埃德蒙·萨努加-巴克的英国研究员。

sentences.en: I've always had an inquiring mind about everything in life.
sentences.zh: 我一生中对任何事情都保持着好奇心。

sentences.en: I tend to be on the side of the questioner rather than the conformist, for sure.
sentences.zh: 我肯定更倾向于做一个质疑者，而不是随波逐流的人。

sentences.en: He was always a really fascinating guy to talk to.
sentences.zh: 他一直是一个谈吐非常迷人的人。

sentences.en: And I think partly because he's kind of an iconoclaSt.
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因是他有点像个反传统者。

sentences.en: Really hardcore punk.
sentences.zh: 非常硬核的朋克。

sentences.en: Like, when he was a teenager, he was in one of the first English punk rock bands.
sentences.zh: 比如，他十几岁时，是英国最早的朋克摇滚乐队之一的成员。

sentences.en: And he still is really someone who just questions the conventional wisdom.
sentences.zh: 而且他至今仍然是一个质疑传统观念的人。

sentences.en: I was at the pub last night.
sentences.zh: 我昨晚在酒吧。

sentences.en: Our conversations would sometimes go off on these long tangents.
sentences.zh: 我们的谈话有时会偏离主题，扯得很远。

sentences.en: Our cricket team played.
sentences.zh: 我们的板球队比赛了。

sentences.en: We went to the pub.
sentences.zh: 我们去了酒吧。

sentences.en: I like to smoke cigars.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢抽雪茄。

sentences.en: So I got to smoke him a cigar.
sentences.zh: 所以我给他点了一支雪茄。

sentences.en: And the lady from the bar, who I know very well, came out.
sentences.zh: 酒吧的那位女士，我非常熟悉，她走了出来。

sentences.en: And she said, well, you can't smoke here.
sentences.zh: 她说，你不能在这里抽烟。

sentences.en: I said, why not?
sentences.zh: 我说，为什么不能？

sentences.en: She said, there's a big sign.
sentences.zh: 她说，那里有个大牌子。

sentences.en: It says, no smoking.
sentences.zh: 上面写着，禁止吸烟。

sentences.en: And I said to her, the bigger the sign, the more likely I am to ignore it.
sentences.zh: 我对她说，牌子越大，我越想无视它。

sentences.en: And I'm afraid that's the way it's been in my career.
sentences.zh: 恐怕我的职业生涯一直就是这样。

sentences.en: Edmund has spent his whole life trying to understand ADHD.
sentences.zh: 埃德蒙一生都在试图理解ADHD。

sentences.en: And part of that is professional, but part of it is personal.
sentences.zh: 这部分是出于职业需要，但部分也是出于个人原因。

sentences.en: He was diagnosed with ADHD back before they were even calling it that.
sentences.zh: 他在人们甚至还没给它命名之前就被诊断出患有ADHD了。

sentences.en: They called it hyperkinesis.
sentences.zh: 他们当时称之为多动症（hyperkinesis）。

sentences.en: There was no real treatment for that in them days.
sentences.zh: 在那个年代，并没有真正的治疗方法。

sentences.en: Not in the UK anyway.
sentences.zh: 至少在英国没有。

sentences.en: People weren't taking medication for hyperkinetic disorder.
sentences.zh: 人们当时并不服用药物来治疗多动障碍。

sentences.en: This is around 1970.
sentences.zh: 那大约是在1970年。

sentences.en: He was living in this working class town in the English Midlands.
sentences.zh: 他当时住在英格兰中部的一个工人阶级城镇。

sentences.en: He's eight years old, misbehaving young kid.
sentences.zh: 他是个八岁的孩子，是个调皮捣蛋的小孩。

sentences.en: Couldn't really sit still.
sentences.zh: 真的坐不住。

sentences.en: And at that clinic anyway, they just sort of told him, you've got this.
sentences.zh: 反正在那家诊所，他们只是告诉他，你得了这个病。

sentences.en: But they didn't do anything to help him.
sentences.zh: 但他们并没有采取任何措施来帮助他。

sentences.en: And so I just went to school.
sentences.zh: 所以我只好去上学了。

sentences.en: And they put me in the remedial class.
sentences.zh: 他们把我放进了补习班。

sentences.en: And I've got this memory.
sentences.zh: 我还有这段记忆。

sentences.en: I've got this image, this memory of them giving me shapes to draw around.
sentences.zh: 我脑海里有这样一个画面，一段记忆，他们给我一些形状让我照着画。

sentences.en: Like squares and triangles.
sentences.zh: 比如正方形和三角形。

sentences.en: Because I couldn't, you know, I couldn't really write.
sentences.zh: 因为我不能，你知道，我真的不会写字。

sentences.en: So they just gave me things to draw around.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只是给我一些东西让我照着画。

sentences.en: He just had a kind of miserable time in school.
sentences.zh: 他在学校里过得很痛苦。

sentences.en: Looking back, I was always in trouble.
sentences.zh: 回首往事，我总是惹麻烦。

sentences.en: I was quite a naughty boy.
sentences.zh: 我曾是个相当淘气的男孩。

sentences.en: And a naughty adolescent.
sentences.zh: 也是个淘气的青少年。

sentences.en: And I think that was a mask.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是一种伪装。

sentences.en: That was a camouflage.
sentences.zh: 那是一种掩护。

sentences.en: I found the setting where I could hide, you know, my weaknesses.
sentences.zh: 我找到了一个可以隐藏我弱点的地方。

sentences.en: Edmund says it was a miracle that he ever made it through high school.
sentences.zh: 埃德蒙说，他能读完高中简直是个奇迹。

sentences.en: But then after high school, because of a few lucky breaks, he gets into a university.
sentences.zh: 但高中毕业后，由于几次幸运的机会，他进入了一所大学。

sentences.en: To Bangor University in Wales.
sentences.zh: 去了威尔士的班戈大学。

sentences.en: And from there, eventually he devotes his life to studying ADHD.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，他最终致力于研究ADHD。

sentences.en: To trying to figure out exactly how it works.
sentences.zh: 试图弄清楚它到底是如何运作的。

sentences.en: I mean, I've invested 35 years of my life trying to identify the causes of ADHD.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我投入了35年的生命试图找出ADHD的成因。

sentences.en: And what we've found is that somehow we seem to be further away from our goal than we were when we started the journey.
sentences.zh: 而我们发现的是，我们似乎离目标比刚开始这段旅程时更远了。

sentences.en: But in recent years, he has really begun to rethink a lot of the work that he's done and rethink the way that we think and talk about ADHD.
sentences.zh: 但近年来，他确实开始重新思考他所做的大量工作，并重新思考我们思考和谈论ADHD的方式。

sentences.en: And what I also found out was that he's not alone.
sentences.zh: 而且我还发现，他并不孤单。

sentences.en: There are other researchers who are also rethinking the research that led us here.
sentences.zh: 还有其他研究人员也在重新思考那些引导我们走到这一步的研究。

sentences.en: This sounds like some pretty profound and personal soul-searching from Edmund and his peers in the field.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是埃德蒙和他的同行们在进行深刻而个人的灵魂拷问。

sentences.en: Potentially with broad implications for how we're thinking about ADHD.
sentences.zh: 这可能对我们如何看待ADHD有着广泛的影响。

sentences.en: So I'm curious, what are they actually rethinking?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，他们到底在重新思考什么？

sentences.en: Well, I would say they fit into two big categories.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想他们可以归纳为两大类。

sentences.en: Some of them are rethinking some of the basic questions of what the definition of ADHD is.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人正在重新思考关于ADHD定义的某些基本问题。

sentences.en: Is it something that is a categorical, biological condition where we can clearly say, like, this person has ADHD and this person does not?
sentences.zh: 它是一种分类明确的生物学疾病吗？我们可以清楚地说，这个人有ADHD，而那个人没有？

sentences.en: Or is it something that's more like a continuum where the lines between a person with ADHD and a person without are not so clear and distinct?
sentences.zh: 还是说它更像是一个连续体，患有ADHD的人和没有ADHD的人之间的界限并不那么清晰和明确？

sentences.en: And then the other group is thinking about our treatment and specifically the treatment with stimulant medications like Ritalin and Adderall.
sentences.zh: 另一组人则在思考我们的治疗方法，特别是使用利他林（Ritalin）和阿德拉（Adderall）等兴奋剂药物的治疗。

sentences.en: Okay, so it sounds like treatment and diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 好的，听起来涉及治疗和诊断。

sentences.en: So kind of the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 所以几乎是整个事情。

sentences.en: Let's start with how they're thinking about diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 让我们从他们如何看待诊断开始吧。

sentences.en: First of all, can you just walk me through how do we diagnose ADHD?
sentences.zh: 首先，你能带我了解一下我们是如何诊断ADHD的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So there is this checklist of symptoms that doctors look at when they want to diagnose ADHD.
sentences.zh: 医生在想要诊断ADHD时，会参考一份症状清单。

sentences.en: And the symptoms are laid out in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders.
sentences.zh: 这些症状列在《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》中。

sentences.en: And in order to diagnose ADHD,
sentences.zh: 为了诊断ADHD，

sentences.en: a clinician has to count a certain number of symptoms in a certain number of settings over a certain number of months with a certain level of impairment.
sentences.zh: 临床医生必须在一定数量的环境中，在一定的时间跨度内，统计出一定数量的症状，并达到一定的损害程度。

sentences.en: Can you give us a little flavor of what's on that checklist?
sentences.zh: 你能简单介绍一下那份清单上有什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, one of the things that is complicated about the ADHD diagnosis is that there are two large categories of symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，ADHD诊断复杂的原因之一是症状分为两大类。

sentences.en: And they often seem pretty different.
sentences.zh: 而且它们看起来往往非常不同。

sentences.en: So there is one category that's about hyperactivity and impulsiveness, things like not being able to wait your turn, not being able to sit in your seat, interrupting people.
sentences.zh: 一类是关于多动和冲动，比如无法等待轮到自己、无法坐在座位上、打断别人说话。

sentences.en: And then the other category is inattentive ADHD.
sentences.zh: 另一类是注意力不集中型ADHD。

sentences.en: And those often look very different than the hyperactive and impulsive kids.
sentences.zh: 这些孩子看起来往往与多动和冲动的孩子非常不同。

sentences.en: Those are often like they don't say anything when you speak to them.
sentences.zh: 他们通常表现为当你跟他们说话时，他们什么都不说。

sentences.en: They're sort of dreamy.
sentences.zh: 他们有点像在做梦。

sentences.en: They are losing things.
sentences.zh: 他们总是丢东西。

sentences.en: They're not able to sustain their attention.
sentences.zh: 他们无法维持注意力。

sentences.en: And so you can often have two kids who are diagnosed with ADHD who might, from appearances, seem very different.
sentences.zh: 所以你经常会看到两个被诊断为ADHD的孩子，从外表上看，他们可能非常不同。

sentences.en: And to me, what that does is it highlights this conflict within the field, which is that on the one hand, these are supposed to be really clear, empirical,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这凸显了该领域内部的这种冲突，即一方面，这些本应是非常清晰、经验性的、

sentences.en: objective definitions of a certain disorder, something that you either have or you don't.
sentences.zh: 客观的某种疾病定义，即你要么有，要么没有。

sentences.en: But on the other, there's a lot of subjectivity involved.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，其中涉及很多主观性。

sentences.en: So put it another way, it sounds like this is actually not a simple diagnosis to make because these children can have the same condition but exhibit very different behaviors.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，听起来这实际上并不是一个简单的诊断，因为这些孩子可能患有相同的疾病，但表现出的行为却大相径庭。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there are other reasons, I think, that it is difficult to diagnose, including the fact that some of these symptoms are actually also symptoms of other things.
sentences.zh: 我认为还有其他原因导致它难以诊断，包括其中一些症状实际上也是其他疾病的症状。

sentences.en: They can be symptoms of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 它们可能是焦虑症的症状。

sentences.en: They can be symptoms of early trauma.
sentences.zh: 它们可能是早期创伤的症状。

sentences.en: And I think that makes for a really challenging diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 我认为这使得诊断变得非常具有挑战性。

sentences.en: And that challenge is part of why the field has been looking for what they call a biomarker, a biological indicator of whether a child has ADHD or does not.
sentences.zh: 这种挑战是该领域一直在寻找所谓“生物标志物”的原因之一，即判断一个孩子是否患有ADHD的生物学指标。

sentences.en: And I think there were a couple of motivations behind this search for an ADHD biomarker, in part, like as a diagnostic tool, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为寻找ADHD生物标志物背后有几个动机，部分是为了作为一种诊断工具，对吧？

sentences.en: If you could just put a kid in an MRI or something to measure their brainwaves and say this child has ADHD, that would be really helpful.
sentences.zh: 如果你能让孩子做个核磁共振或测量一下脑电波，就能说这个孩子患有ADHD，那将非常有帮助。

sentences.en: It would eliminate a lot of the subjectivity that we've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 这将消除我们一直在讨论的许多主观性。

sentences.en: But the other reason, I think, was to shore up the legitimacy of the diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 但我认为另一个原因是巩固诊断的合法性。

sentences.en: There always have been skeptics who just say, like, ADHD is not even a thing.
sentences.zh: 一直以来都有怀疑论者说，ADHD根本不存在。

sentences.en: Like, it's just a made-up diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 就像说这只是一个编造出来的诊断。

sentences.en: These are just rambunctious kids.
sentences.zh: 这些只是顽皮的孩子。

sentences.en: There is no such thing.
sentences.zh: 根本没有这种病。

sentences.en: And that's very frustrating, I think, for researchers who can see the great problems that a lot of kids have and see the medications are really helping them.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对研究人员来说非常令人沮丧，因为他们能看到许多孩子面临的巨大问题，也能看到药物确实在帮助他们。

sentences.en: And so to find a biomarker, to find something where they could say, look, it's real.
sentences.zh: 所以找到一个生物标志物，找到某种东西让他们能说，看，它是真实的。

sentences.en: It's something very specific that you can see in this brain.
sentences.zh: 这是你在大脑中能看到的非常具体的东西。

sentences.en: This is a brain disorder.
sentences.zh: 这是一种脑部疾病。

sentences.en: And it's something with clear boundaries.
sentences.zh: 而且它有着明确的界限。

sentences.en: I think that was very appealing to the field as well.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对该领域也很有吸引力。

sentences.en: Like, this is a brain disorder.
sentences.zh: 比如，这是一种脑部疾病。

sentences.en: This is not just kids behaving badly.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是孩子表现不好。

sentences.en: This is not just bad parenting.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是家教不当。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It is something deep in the brain that we can track, we can measure, and we can diagnose.
sentences.zh: 它是大脑深处某种我们可以追踪、测量并诊断的东西。

sentences.en: So tell me about the search for that biomarker and how it has contributed to the soul searching in the field.
sentences.zh: 那么，请跟我谈谈对这种生物标志物的寻找，以及它如何促成了该领域的自我反思。

sentences.en: So in the very early 2000s was the period, I think, of the greatest optimism about this.
sentences.zh: 我认为，21世纪初是对此最乐观的时期。

sentences.en: This was an era in a lot of breakthroughs in genetics, especially.
sentences.zh: 那是一个遗传学领域取得许多突破的时代，尤其是遗传学。

sentences.en: And in lots of different conditions, there was this belief that we were going to find the one gene that predicted each of these disorders, and certainly including ADHD.
sentences.zh: 在许多不同的病症中，人们都相信我们会找到预测每种疾病的单一基因，当然也包括多动症（ADHD）。

sentences.en: There were early signs that there were these electrical signals that seemed like they predicted ADHD, signs from MRIs as well.
sentences.zh: 早期有一些迹象表明，存在一些似乎能预测多动症的电信号，核磁共振成像（MRI）也有相关迹象。

sentences.en: But then, as the 2000s went on, a lot of those early experiments didn't hold up when larger, better studies were done with more sophisticated technology.
sentences.zh: 但随着21世纪的推进，当使用更先进的技术进行更大规模、更完善的研究时，许多早期的实验结果都站不住脚了。

sentences.en: And one by one, each of those early indications of a potential biomarker sort of fell apart.
sentences.zh: 一个接一个，那些早期关于潜在生物标志物的迹象都破灭了。

sentences.en: So the brainwave studies, when we got better equipment, no, there were no real brainwave differences between kids with a diagnosis and kids without.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们有了更好的设备进行脑电波研究时，结果发现，确诊儿童和未确诊儿童之间并没有真正的脑电波差异。

sentences.en: Genetics, as happened with lots of other psychiatric conditions, it was clear that there was no single gene that predicted ADHD.
sentences.zh: 至于遗传学，正如许多其他精神疾病一样，很明显没有单一基因可以预测多动症。

sentences.en: And then there was this really ambitious attempt to confirm those early MRI studies.
sentences.zh: 然后，人们进行了一次非常雄心勃勃的尝试，试图证实那些早期的核磁共振研究。

sentences.en: It was done by this big international network of neuroscientists and psychiatrists called the Enigma Consortium.
sentences.zh: 这是由一个名为“Enigma联盟”的国际神经科学家和精神科医生大型网络完成的。

sentences.en: They had this database of 4,000 brain scans that they were able to look at.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有一个包含4000份脑部扫描的数据库可供研究。

sentences.en: And they were able to, in this really detailed way, compare the brains of people with ADHD diagnoses and people without.
sentences.zh: 他们能够以非常详细的方式，比较确诊多动症患者和未确诊者的大脑。

sentences.en: But when they finished looking at all of the data from all of those scans, they found that actually they weren't seeing much of anything.
sentences.zh: 但当他们看完所有扫描数据后，发现实际上并没有看到什么显著差异。

sentences.en: In adults and in adolescents, they didn't see any difference in the brains of people with and without the diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 在成人和青少年中，他们没有发现确诊者和未确诊者的大脑有任何区别。

sentences.en: And in children, there was a small difference, but a really, really small difference.
sentences.zh: 而在儿童中，存在微小的差异，但真的非常非常小。

sentences.en: And just to be clear, though, what you have just described, does that mean that there is no biomarker or does it mean that we just haven't found one yet?
sentences.zh: 为了明确起见，你刚才描述的情况，是指不存在生物标志物，还是说我们只是还没找到？

sentences.en: It means we haven't found one yet, but it also means we probably won't find one that is as simple and clear as we'd hoped.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们还没找到，但也意味着我们可能永远找不到像我们希望的那样简单明了的标志物。

sentences.en: Basically, what we thought was there isn't really there.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我们以为存在的东西其实并不存在。

sentences.en: And this is frustrating for the researchers involved, including Edmund.
sentences.zh: 这对参与研究的学者来说很令人沮丧，包括埃德蒙（Edmund）。

sentences.en: He devoted many years to looking for biomarkers, and he basically thinks now that it was all a mistake.
sentences.zh: 他花了多年时间寻找生物标志物，现在他基本上认为那完全是个错误。

sentences.en: Chasing this biomarker has been such a red herring for the field that it's taken us in the totally wrong direction.
sentences.zh: 追寻这种生物标志物对该领域来说是一个巨大的误导，它把我们带向了完全错误的方向。

sentences.en: And now he's really, I think, turned away from just focusing narrowly on the biology of ADHD.
sentences.zh: 我认为他现在已经不再仅仅狭隘地关注多动症的生物学层面了。

sentences.en: I'm not saying it's not biological.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说它没有生物学基础。

sentences.en: I'm just saying I don't think that's the proper target, really, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 我只是说，老实讲，我不认为那是正确的切入点。

sentences.en: So basically, we're no closer to understanding what ADHD is now than we were back when we first started searching for a biomarker.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，我们现在对多动症的理解，并不比我们刚开始寻找生物标志物时更深入。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And the other place I think that started to have an effect is in our thinking about treatment.
sentences.zh: 我认为另一个开始产生影响的地方是我们的治疗思路。

sentences.en: I mean, if this is not a clear, you know, black and white medical condition, is a medical treatment, a pharmaceutical, the best way to treat it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果这不是一种明确的、非黑即白的医疗状况，那么药物治疗是最好的方式吗？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是Wynna Liu。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是Sam Azersky，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: So, Paul, before the break, you mentioned that researchers were just starting to re-examine the role of medication in treating ADHD.
sentences.zh: 那么，保罗（Paul），在休息之前，你提到研究人员刚开始重新审视药物在治疗多动症中的作用。

sentences.en: I'm very curious about the medication itself, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我对药物本身非常好奇。

sentences.en: Can you talk a little bit about what medication we're talking about and how we even came to it?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈我们所说的药物是什么，以及我们是如何使用它们的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So, the main medications that are used to treat ADHD are stimulants, Ritalin and Adderall and other similar medications.
sentences.zh: 用于治疗多动症的主要药物是兴奋剂，如利他林（Ritalin）、阿得拉（Adderall）和其他类似药物。

sentences.en: And there are some chemical differences, but basically they are all derived from amphetamines.
sentences.zh: 它们之间有一些化学差异，但基本上都是从苯丙胺中提取的。

sentences.en: And the way that scientists first got the idea that these might be useful as a way to treat ADHD-like symptoms came way back in the 1930s before anyone had thought of the initials ADHD.
sentences.zh: 科学家们最初想到这些药物可能有助于治疗多动症症状，要追溯到20世纪30年代，那时还没人想到“多动症”这个缩写。

sentences.en: And there was this doctor who ran his own home in Rhode Island for misbehaving kids.
sentences.zh: 当时有一位医生在罗德岛经营着一家收容所，专门收容行为不端的孩子。

sentences.en: And he was trying to figure out what he could do to help them behave better.
sentences.zh: 他试图找出能帮助他们改善行为的方法。

sentences.en: And amphetamines at the time were this kind of recreational drug.
sentences.zh: 当时的苯丙胺是一种娱乐性药物。

sentences.en: Benzedrine was the popular version.
sentences.zh: 苯齐君（Benzedrine）是当时流行的版本。

sentences.en: And so, he just started giving daily doses of Benzedrine to 30 or so kids who were in his home.
sentences.zh: 于是，他开始给收容所里的30个左右的孩子每天服用定量的苯齐君。

sentences.en: And he noticed immediately this kind of miraculous change in these kids that overnight their behaviors improved, their mood improved, they followed the rules better.
sentences.zh: 他立刻注意到这些孩子发生了奇迹般的变化，一夜之间，他们的行为改善了，情绪好转了，也更听话了。

sentences.en: And it just felt like this kind of miracle cure.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像一种奇迹般的疗法。

sentences.en: But what Bradley was doing sounds a bit informal, right?
sentences.zh: 但布拉德利（Bradley）的做法听起来有点非正式，对吧？

sentences.en: Like he's giving amphetamines to kids in this home, essentially, which sounds pretty small scale,
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在给收容所里的孩子服用苯丙胺，这听起来规模很小，

sentences.en: especially when you compare it to the amount of prescriptions that we see out in the world today.
sentences.zh: 特别是当你把它与今天世界上看到的处方量相比时。

sentences.en: So, I'm just sort of curious how we go from what he was doing in the 30s to this explosion that we see in the year 2025.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，我们是如何从他30年代的做法，演变成2025年看到的这种爆发式增长的。

sentences.en: So, we do know a lot more about these stimulant medications than we did back then.
sentences.zh: 我们对这些兴奋剂药物的了解确实比当时多得多。

sentences.en: And there have been some much more sophisticated studies.
sentences.zh: 而且已经进行了一些更复杂的研究。

sentences.en: And the one that I think is the most significant one started out in the early 1990s.
sentences.zh: 我认为最重要的一项研究始于20世纪90年代初。

sentences.en: Between 1990 and 1993, we went from having 1 million kids diagnosed with ADHD to 2 million, a huge rise.
sentences.zh: 在1990年到1993年间，被诊断为多动症的儿童从100万增加到了200万，这是一个巨大的增长。

sentences.en: We're now up to 7 million.
sentences.zh: 现在我们已经达到了700万。

sentences.en: So, things are a lot bigger than they were then.
sentences.zh: 所以，情况比当时严重得多。

sentences.en: But this is like doubling in just a few years.
sentences.zh: 但这就像在短短几年内翻了一番。

sentences.en: And Ritalin was the big stimulant medication.
sentences.zh: 利他林是当时主要的兴奋剂药物。

sentences.en: And so, it was what was being used to treat kids.
sentences.zh: 所以它被用来治疗儿童。

sentences.en: But scientists didn't really know how effective it was.
sentences.zh: 但科学家们并不真正知道它有多有效。

sentences.en: They were seeing the same sort of thing that Charles Bradley saw, that it looked like when you gave this to kids, that their symptoms improved often almost overnight.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了查尔斯·布拉德利（Charles Bradley）看到的同样现象，即给孩子服用这种药后，他们的症状往往几乎一夜之间就改善了。

sentences.en: But they wanted to be more scientific about it.
sentences.zh: 但他们想对此进行更科学的研究。

sentences.en: So, they devised this giant, randomized, controlled study in which they divided hundreds of kids up into different treatment groups.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们设计了一项大型随机对照研究，将数百名儿童分成不同的治疗组。

sentences.en: Some would get a daily dose of Ritalin.
sentences.zh: 一些人每天服用利他林。

sentences.en: Some would get different sorts of behavioral treatments.
sentences.zh: 一些人接受不同类型的行为治疗。

sentences.en: Some would get a combination.
sentences.zh: 一些人接受联合治疗。

sentences.en: And then there was a fourth group where they didn't give them any particular treatments.
sentences.zh: 还有第四组，他们没有接受任何特定的治疗。

sentences.en: They could just figure out their treatment on their own.
sentences.zh: 他们可以自己决定治疗方式。

sentences.en: So, you have a stimulant group, a therapy group, and a kind of control group that was not prescribed any specific treatment at all, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，有一个兴奋剂组、一个治疗组，还有一个没有开具任何特定治疗方案的对照组，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so, they studied it over 14 months.
sentences.zh: 他们研究了14个月。

sentences.en: And at the end of the 14 months, the kids who had taken Ritalin every day were clearly doing better.
sentences.zh: 14个月结束时，每天服用利他林的儿童显然表现更好。

sentences.en: Their symptoms were more reduced than children in any of the other groups.
sentences.zh: 他们的症状比其他任何组的儿童减轻得都多。

sentences.en: And so, that was interpreted as this very clear message that Ritalin worked.
sentences.zh: 因此，这被解读为一个非常明确的信息：利他林有效。

sentences.en: It's the first thing that we should go to.
sentences.zh: 这是我们应该首先考虑的方案。

sentences.en: And that message, I think, went out to doctors' offices and clinics all over the country and all over the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个信息传遍了全国乃至全世界的医生办公室和诊所。

sentences.en: And it certainly seems that that message was well-received just based on the number of prescriptions alone.
sentences.zh: 仅从处方数量来看，这个信息显然很受欢迎。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, during that era, this is now sort of the early 2000s, diagnoses continued to rise and prescriptions continued to rise as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，在那个时代，也就是21世纪初，诊断率和处方量都在持续上升。

sentences.en: But those scientists who had been carefully studying Ritalin compared to these different other treatments,
sentences.zh: 但是那些一直在仔细研究利他林与其他治疗方法对比的科学家们，

sentences.en: they actually continued to follow these children in this study for many years.
sentences.zh: 实际上在研究结束后又对这些孩子进行了多年的跟踪观察。

sentences.en: And what they found was that after three years, the relative benefits of Ritalin faded.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，三年后，利他林的相对益处消失了。

sentences.en: And by the end of those three years, the children in each of these treatment groups were doing exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 到这三年结束时，每个治疗组的孩子表现完全一样。

sentences.en: So, the kids with Ritalin didn't have any advantage in terms of their symptoms over the children who had had the behavioral treatment.
sentences.zh: 所以，服用利他林的孩子在症状方面并没有比接受行为治疗的孩子有任何优势。

sentences.en: They didn't have any real advantage over the ones who had just been left alone to figure out their own treatment.
sentences.zh: 他们与那些被放任自流、自己决定治疗方案的孩子相比，也没有任何真正的优势。

sentences.en: All of the clear benefits that were there at 14 months had disappeared by 36 months.
sentences.zh: 14个月时存在的所有明显益处，到了36个月时都消失了。

sentences.en: That really seems pretty stunning.
sentences.zh: 这看起来确实相当令人震惊。

sentences.en: This idea that this medication that has seen an explosion in prescriptions seems to have no discernible impact.
sentences.zh: 这种处方量激增的药物似乎没有任何明显的影响。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it clearly does have an impact in the short term.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它在短期内显然是有影响的。

sentences.en: But over the long term, this most reliable study found no relative benefit to Ritalin.
sentences.zh: 但从长期来看，这项最可靠的研究发现利他林没有相对益处。

sentences.en: And there were other things that scientists were discovering at the same time.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，科学家们还发现了其他一些事情。

sentences.en: So, one researcher described to me that the really sort of puzzling and discouraging thing for him is that even when we see the effect on symptoms,
sentences.zh: 一位研究人员向我描述，对他来说真正令人困惑和沮丧的是，即使我们看到了症状上的效果，

sentences.en: like that you can sit still in class, that you can, like, pay attention in class, that when you look at academic results, that when we look at sort of cognitive ability,
sentences.zh: 比如你能坐在教室里保持安静，比如你能上课专心听讲，但当你观察学习成绩，当你观察认知能力时，

sentences.en: there doesn't seem to be any corresponding impact, that the kids who take stimulant medications seem to be learning more,
sentences.zh: 似乎没有任何相应的影响，服用兴奋剂的孩子看起来学习更努力了，

sentences.en: but that when you measure their results, they haven't actually learned any more than the kids who didn't take any medication.
sentences.zh: 但当你测量他们的结果时，他们实际上并没有比那些没吃药的孩子学到更多东西。

sentences.en: But can I just ask, I'm curious, like, if the medication is getting kids to do more work, like, I don't know, for example,
sentences.zh: 但我能问一下吗，我很好奇，如果药物让孩子们做了更多的工作，比如，我不知道，举个例子，

sentences.en: just filling out worksheets or multiplication tables or whatever, I mean, isn't part of learning, like, repeating something over and over again?
sentences.zh: 只是填写练习册或乘法表之类的，我的意思是，学习的一部分不就是一遍又一遍地重复吗？

sentences.en: Like, I'm just sort of curious how the exercise of just doing more work that is intended to get you to absorb and learn stuff doesn't actually have that effect.
sentences.zh: 我只是好奇，为什么这种旨在让你吸收和学习知识的额外工作练习，实际上并没有产生那种效果。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think to a lot of researchers, it is a real puzzle.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为对许多研究人员来说，这确实是一个谜。

sentences.en: The research that helped make sense of this for me was another series of studies
sentences.zh: 帮助我理解这一点的研究是另一系列研究，

sentences.en: where researchers gave stimulant medication to a bunch of college students, had them do a bunch of cognitive tests.
sentences.zh: 研究人员给一群大学生服用了兴奋剂，让他们做了一系列认知测试。

sentences.en: Their scores were no better if they had taken the medication or not.
sentences.zh: 无论他们是否服药，他们的分数都没有提高。

sentences.en: But then when they asked them, how did you feel about the work that you just did?
sentences.zh: 但当问他们对刚才所做的工作感觉如何时，

sentences.en: The ones who had taken the medication said that they did better.
sentences.zh: 服药的人说他们做得更好。

sentences.en: They felt better about themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们对自己感觉更好。

sentences.en: They felt better about the answers that they had given.
sentences.zh: 他们对给出的答案感觉更好。

sentences.en: And that connects with other research that shows that the main impact of stimulant medication is on our emotions more than on our cognition.
sentences.zh: 这与其他研究相吻合，表明兴奋剂的主要影响在于我们的情绪，而不是认知。

sentences.en: It makes us feel more motivated, feel more connected with the work that we're doing.
sentences.zh: 它让我们感到更有动力，感到与我们正在做的工作联系更紧密。

sentences.en: Even if it's boring.
sentences.zh: 即使工作很无聊。

sentences.en: Yeah, especially if it's boring.
sentences.zh: 是的，尤其是在工作很无聊的时候。

sentences.en: But I think what this indicates is that even if we think of these sometimes as smart pills,
sentences.zh: 但我认为这表明，即使我们有时把这些药视为“聪明药”，

sentences.en: as things that are affecting our cognition, in reality, what it's affecting is our emotional state.
sentences.zh: 认为它们在影响我们的认知，但实际上，它们影响的是我们的情绪状态。

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds like what you're telling me is that there's no long-term measurable benefit from these drugs,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听起来你是在告诉我，这些药物没有长期的可测量益处，

sentences.en: and that even in the short term, they don't really work to improve academic performance in the way that we thought they did.
sentences.zh: 而且即使在短期内，它们也没有像我们想象的那样有效提高学习成绩。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, when you put it that way, it does sound kind of bad.
sentences.zh: 是的，当你这么说的时候，听起来确实有点糟糕。

sentences.en: But one of the things that strikes me when I talk to these psychiatrists is that they say that compared to other psychiatric medications, these are so good, right?
sentences.zh: 但当我与这些精神科医生交谈时，有一点让我印象深刻，他们说与其他精神科药物相比，这些药非常好，对吧？

sentences.en: Like they do a pretty good job, at least in the short term, of helping kids manage their symptoms, remain calm in class.
sentences.zh: 它们在短期内确实能很好地帮助孩子控制症状，在课堂上保持冷静。

sentences.en: And they're so much more effective than, you know, antidepressants or a lot of anti-anxiety or anti-psychotic medications.
sentences.zh: 而且它们比抗抑郁药或许多抗焦虑、抗精神病药物有效得多。

sentences.en: They have fewer side effects.
sentences.zh: 它们的副作用更少。

sentences.en: And most importantly, I think they're easy to stop.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，我认为它们很容易停药。

sentences.en: So a lot of psychiatric medications, when you take them, it takes a while for them to start working in your brain.
sentences.zh: 很多精神科药物，当你服用时，需要一段时间才能在大脑中起效。

sentences.en: And then if you want to stop, it takes a while to wean off them.
sentences.zh: 如果你想停药，也需要一段时间来逐渐减量。

sentences.en: But if Ritalin or Adderall isn't working for you, you can just stop and it leaves your system almost right away.
sentences.zh: 但如果利他林或阿得拉对你无效，你可以直接停药，它几乎会立即排出体外。

sentences.en: So from their point of view, low risk, high reward.
sentences.zh: 所以从他们的角度来看，低风险，高回报。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: But there must be some side effects, right?
sentences.zh: 但肯定会有一些副作用，对吧？

sentences.en: Like every medication has side effects.
sentences.zh: 就像每种药物都有副作用一样。

sentences.en: So did these researchers find any downsides?
sentences.zh: 那么这些研究人员有没有发现什么负面影响？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: So in this big randomized controlled study, they did find some significant downsides.
sentences.zh: 在这项大型随机对照研究中，他们确实发现了一些显著的负面影响。

sentences.en: And the main one was about the effect of stimulant medications on height, on growth.
sentences.zh: 主要的一点是关于兴奋剂对身高和生长发育的影响。

sentences.en: So this was something they weren't expecting.
sentences.zh: 这是他们没预料到的。

sentences.en: But in that first study, when they looked at the different groups after 36 months,
sentences.zh: 但在那项最初的研究中，当他们观察36个月后的不同组别时，

sentences.en: the ones who had taken stimulant medication consistently were about an inch shorter than the ones who had either started and stopped or hadn't taken the medication at all.
sentences.zh: 那些一直服用兴奋剂类药物的人，比那些开始服用后又停药或从未服药的人，身高大约矮了一英寸。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: And now, you know, the same scientists have continued to follow this group for decades.
sentences.zh: 现在，你知道，同一批科学家几十年来一直在跟踪研究这个群体。

sentences.en: And that height disparity hasn't gone away.
sentences.zh: 而且这种身高差距并没有消失。

sentences.en: I feel like most people would want that inch.
sentences.zh: 我觉得大多数人都会想要那一英寸的身高。

sentences.en: And I have to say, Paul, that's actually not what I thought you were going to say the downside was.
sentences.zh: 保罗，我不得不说，这其实并不是我以为你会说的负面影响。

sentences.en: Like, I thought you were going to talk about these drugs being addictive because, frankly,
sentences.zh: 比如，我以为你会谈论这些药物的成瘾性，因为坦白说，

sentences.en: I just feel like I know people who may be in college or law school or whenever they became really dependent on these medications.
sentences.zh: 我感觉我认识一些人，可能是在上大学或法学院时，或者在某个阶段，他们对这些药物产生了严重的依赖。

sentences.en: And they did have a hard time getting off of them.
sentences.zh: 而且他们确实很难戒掉这些药。

sentences.en: And I know that that's just very anecdotal and not data.
sentences.zh: 我知道这只是非常主观的个人经验，并非数据。

sentences.en: But is that an issue here?
sentences.zh: 但这在这里是个问题吗？

sentences.en: Do researchers think that these medications have addictive properties at all?
sentences.zh: 研究人员认为这些药物完全具有成瘾性吗？

sentences.en: I think we're not sure.
sentences.zh: 我想我们还不确定。

sentences.en: So I think, you know, absolutely for certain people, for certain personalities, certainly recreational amphetamines can be addictive.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，你知道，对于某些人、某些性格来说，娱乐性地使用安非他命绝对是会成瘾的。

sentences.en: And I think for some kids and teenagers, even prescribed Ritalin or Adderall can be habit forming.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为对于一些孩子和青少年来说，即使是处方药利他林或阿德拉尔也可能让人产生依赖。

sentences.en: When you look at the data as a whole, these medications don't lead to more addictive behaviors.
sentences.zh: 但当你纵观整体数据时，这些药物并不会导致更多的成瘾行为。

sentences.en: And, in fact, one of the things that I really heard when I talked to teenagers who had been taking Ritalin or Adderall for a while is that it was kind of the opposite.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我采访那些服用利他林或阿德拉尔一段时间的青少年时，我听到的一件事恰恰相反。

sentences.en: It wasn't that it was habit forming.
sentences.zh: 并不是说它让人上瘾。

sentences.en: They didn't really like it.
sentences.zh: 他们其实并不喜欢它。

sentences.en: They just didn't like the way that it made them feel.
sentences.zh: 他们只是不喜欢这种药带给他们的感觉。

sentences.en: They would take it because they saw benefits or because, you know, their parents or their teachers were telling them that they should.
sentences.zh: 他们服用它是因为他们看到了好处，或者是因为，你知道，他们的父母或老师告诉他们应该服用。

sentences.en: But most of them just couldn't wait to get off it.
sentences.zh: 但他们大多数人只是迫不及待地想停药。

sentences.en: And when they had an opportunity, they would.
sentences.zh: 一旦有机会，他们就会停药。

sentences.en: So, Paul, where does the research and the work go from here?
sentences.zh: 那么，保罗，这项研究和工作接下来该往哪个方向发展呢？

sentences.en: Like, how are the people who are studying this condition right now thinking about ADHD and how to treat it, given everything that you've just laid out?
sentences.zh: 比如，考虑到你刚才所阐述的一切，现在研究这种疾病的人是如何看待多动症（ADHD）以及如何治疗它的？

sentences.en: One of the things that's interesting to me is that they're often not saying that we need to diagnose ADHD any differently or treat it any differently.
sentences.zh: 有趣的一点是，他们通常并不是说我们需要以不同的方式诊断或治疗多动症。

sentences.en: They're just saying we should think about it differently.
sentences.zh: 他们只是说我们应该以不同的方式去思考它。

sentences.en: And a lot of that starts with thinking about the world surrounding kids more than just thinking about what's going on in their brains.
sentences.zh: 而这很大程度上始于更多地去思考孩子周围的世界，而不是仅仅盯着他们大脑里发生了什么。

sentences.en: And that gets me back to Edmund.
sentences.zh: 这就让我回到了埃德蒙的话题上。

sentences.en: So he is the scientist who I think is thinking about this stuff in the most interesting ways.
sentences.zh: 他是我认为以最有趣的方式思考这些问题的科学家。

sentences.en: And for him, this idea links back to his own childhood.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，这个想法可以追溯到他自己的童年。

sentences.en: But I always remember thinking, why don't people think like me when I was at school?
sentences.zh: 但我总是记得我在想，为什么我在学校时，人们不像我这样思考？

sentences.en: Why don't people think like me?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们不像我这样思考？

sentences.en: Like I mentioned at the beginning, he was a terrible high school student, terrible at the kind of, you know, sitting still, switching from one topic to another,
sentences.zh: 就像我开头提到的，他是个糟糕的高中生，不擅长那种，你知道，静坐、从一个话题切换到另一个话题，

sentences.en: doing exactly what you're told.
sentences.zh: 完全按照别人的要求去做。

sentences.en: But it turns out he's actually kind of a great university student.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，他其实是个很棒的大学生。

sentences.en: So it was like day and night compared to what I was like before.
sentences.zh: 所以这和他以前的样子简直是天壤之别。

sentences.en: He had this thing that he now calls hyper-focus, that to his teachers back in Darby just looked like, you know, mind-wandering.
sentences.zh: 他有一种现在被称为“超专注”的能力，但在他达比的老师们看来，那只是，你知道，走神。

sentences.en: But that actually, when you're trying to get deep on a subject the way you do in university, it was really functional.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，当你像在大学里那样试图深入钻研一个课题时，这种能力非常实用。

sentences.en: And I did nine to five every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天朝九晚五地学习。

sentences.en: So I'd go to the library, you know, even half eight in the morning.
sentences.zh: 我会去图书馆，你知道，甚至早上八点半就去。

sentences.en: I'd sit in the library, get all the books out, all the journals out, and I'd work through to five o'clock.
sentences.zh: 我坐在图书馆里，把所有的书、所有的期刊都拿出来，一直学习到五点钟。

sentences.en: And so he would just start going to the library and studying hard and suddenly found his identity as a scholar.
sentences.zh: 于是他开始去图书馆努力学习，突然找到了作为学者的自我认同。

sentences.en: So instead of feeling like the failure, the bad kid, the kid who was always in trouble, he suddenly was getting positive reinforcement and good feedback and like, oh,
sentences.zh: 所以，他不再觉得自己是个失败者、坏孩子，或者总是惹麻烦的孩子，他突然得到了积极的强化和良好的反馈，就像，噢，

sentences.en: this thing that happens in my brain turns out to be really useful in this particular setting.
sentences.zh: 原来我大脑里发生的这种事情，在这个特定的环境中竟然非常有用。

sentences.en: He thinks that maybe the best way to think about ADHD is as this mismatch,
sentences.zh: 他认为，看待多动症最好的方式或许是将其视为一种错位，

sentences.en: this misalignment between the specific brain of a young person and the environment in which they're living.
sentences.zh: 即年轻人的特定大脑与他们所处环境之间的不匹配。

sentences.en: The idea of ADHD that you are describing sounds kind of situationally dependent, like something that works for you in one context could work against you in another context.
sentences.zh: 你所描述的多动症概念听起来有点取决于具体情况，就像在一种环境下对你有用的东西，在另一种环境下可能会适得其反。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Not this kind of fixed idea of a condition you just have or don't have, but something more transitory or mutable.
sentences.zh: 这不是一种关于你是否患有某种疾病的固定观念，而是一种更具过渡性或可变性的东西。

sentences.en: And looking back on this experience now, even including being really miserable in school when he was a kid, he thinks that if he had received medication as a kid,
sentences.zh: 现在回首这段经历，即使包括他小时候在学校里过得非常痛苦，他认为如果他小时候接受过药物治疗，

sentences.en: his life might not have turned out this way.
sentences.zh: 他的人生可能就不会是现在这样了。

sentences.en: This must be a question for you.
sentences.zh: 这一定是个值得你思考的问题。

sentences.en: Like, how would life be different if you were in a different, had grown up in a different era or in a different town and had been diagnosed and prescribed Adderall?
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你生活在不同的时代，或者在不同的城镇长大，并且被诊断出患有多动症并开了阿德拉尔，生活会有什么不同？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's a very, I think it's a very, what would be lost?
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这是一个非常，我想这是一个非常，会有什么损失呢？

sentences.en: I think I couldn't have gained anything.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我可能什么也得不到。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I might have gained peace of mind.
sentences.zh: 我可能会获得内心的平静。

sentences.en: I'm a worrier, you know, you know, I got all these, I have a lot of, my mind is constantly, I mean, that, the thing is exhausting, really.
sentences.zh: 我是一个爱操心的人，你知道，你知道，我有所有这些，我有很多，我的大脑一直在，我的意思是，那，那件事真的很让人精疲力竭。

sentences.en: I'm constantly churning away, thinking of things and, you know, I never relax.
sentences.zh: 我一直在不停地运转，思考各种事情，而且，你知道，我从不放松。

sentences.en: So I suppose that's the thing I would, I'd like to be able to relax.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜这就是我想要的，我想能够放松一下。

sentences.en: The only time I relax is when I'm dancing.
sentences.zh: 我唯一放松的时候就是跳舞的时候。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I love dancing.
sentences.zh: 我热爱跳舞。

sentences.en: I'm a big dancer.
sentences.zh: 我是个狂热的舞者。

sentences.en: I still like dancing.
sentences.zh: 我依然喜欢跳舞。

sentences.en: So I would have liked to be able to relax a bit more.
sentences.zh: 所以我本来会希望能够多放松一点。

sentences.en: Maybe that would have done that.
sentences.zh: 也许药物能做到这一点。

sentences.en: Maybe it wouldn't have done that.
sentences.zh: 也许它做不到。

sentences.en: What do you think you would have lost?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你会失去什么？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But in my particular case, there's a lot of characteristics that have helped.
sentences.zh: 但在我个人的案例中，有很多特征对我有所帮助。

sentences.en: I do believe the speed at which I think about things, the amount of things I think about, my ability.
sentences.zh: 我确实相信我思考问题的速度、我思考的事情的数量，我的能力。

sentences.en: And we didn't mention it last time.
sentences.zh: 我们上次没提到这一点。

sentences.en: But what he says is that he thinks that he learned some skills, some different ways of coping that have turned out to be really helpful for him.
sentences.zh: 但他所说的是，他认为他学到了一些技能，一些不同的应对方式，这些对他来说非常有帮助。

sentences.en: I am curious, though, how Edmund feels about medication, given all of this.
sentences.zh: 不过，我很好奇，考虑到这一切，埃德蒙对药物治疗有什么看法？

sentences.en: Like, does he think that there is a role for medication?
sentences.zh: 比如，他认为药物治疗有其作用吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, he absolutely does.
sentences.zh: 是的，他绝对认为有。

sentences.en: All the people I know whose kids have taken medication for ADHD, it was appropriate, and it's helped improve outcomes.
sentences.zh: 我认识的所有孩子服用过治疗多动症药物的人，都认为那是合适的，而且确实改善了结果。

sentences.en: He thinks that the problem is seeing ADHD as a medical problem with a medical cure, and that cure is stimulant medication.
sentences.zh: 他认为问题在于将多动症视为一个医学问题，并试图用医学手段来治愈，而这种“治愈”就是兴奋剂药物。

sentences.en: It's not a silver bullet.
sentences.zh: 它不是万灵药。

sentences.en: It never will be.
sentences.zh: 永远也不会是。

sentences.en: One of the things that he says is that for young people, for kids and for teenagers, one of the best things that medication can do is it can give a family a kind of a break.
sentences.zh: 他提到的一点是，对于年轻人、孩子和青少年来说，药物能做的最好的事情之一就是给家庭一个喘息的机会。

sentences.en: The way I see medication, really, I suppose,
sentences.zh: 我真正看待药物的方式，我想，

sentences.en: is it's a window for parents then to re-engage with their kids or to teach it to re-engage with the child and to do the important work from there,
sentences.zh: 是它为父母提供了一个窗口，让他们能够重新与孩子建立联系，或者教导他们重新与孩子互动，并从那里开始做重要的工作，

sentences.en: rather than as a medical solution to a medical disorder.
sentences.zh: 而不是将其视为一种针对医学疾病的医学解决方案。

sentences.en: That when you're in a family that is in a crisis, when a kid is constantly losing lunchboxes and forgetting homework, and that's all you talk about,
sentences.zh: 当一个家庭处于危机之中，当一个孩子不断弄丢饭盒、忘记做作业，而你们谈论的全部内容就是这些，

sentences.en: all you're doing is just yelling at each other about these things, that medication, because it does, for most kids, have this powerful effect, at least in the short term,
sentences.zh: 你们所做的只是为了这些事情互相大喊大叫时，药物——因为它对大多数孩子来说，至少在短期内对症状有这种强大的效果——可以让你从那些争吵中解脱出来。

sentences.en: on symptoms, it can give you a break from those quarrels.
sentences.zh: 它能给你多一点空间去思考，比如，我们该如何处理这件事？

sentences.en: And it can allow you a little bit more space to say, like, how do we want to deal with this?
sentences.zh: 它创造了一个空间，让人们可以重新建立联系，重新发展关系，诸如此类。

sentences.en: It kind of just creates a space where people can reconnect, redevelop relationships, so forth and so on.
sentences.zh: 我想他会说，问题在于许多家庭在这一步就停止了对话，他们把药物视为治愈方法，视为终点。

sentences.en: And I think what he would say is that the problem is that a lot of families stop their conversations there, that they look at the medication as the cure, as the end point.
sentences.zh: 而他希望我们将其视为对话的开始，

sentences.en: And he wants us to think of it as the beginning of a conversation,
sentences.zh: 去思考这个年轻人的大脑与他们所处环境之间的错位到底是怎么回事，并找出前进的道路。

sentences.en: to think about what is going on with the misalignment between this young person's brain and the environment that they're in, and to figure out what the path forward is.
sentences.zh: 也许那条路继续是药物治疗。

sentences.en: And maybe that continues to be medication.
sentences.zh: 也许药物是长期的答案，但也可能不是。

sentences.en: Maybe medication is the answer for the long term, but maybe not.
sentences.zh: 也许现在情况稍微平静了一些，你可以做出其他改变，从长远来看会有更好的帮助。

sentences.en: Maybe there are other changes that you can make, now that things are a little calmer, that will help better in the long term.
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 他说，重要的是多动症症状患者的真实体验。

sentences.en: What he says is that what matters is the actual experience that people with ADHD symptoms are having.
sentences.zh: 你看，我认为最重要的事情，这是发自内心的，是自我厌恶和低自尊。

sentences.en: See, I think the biggest thing, and this is heartfelt, is self-hatred and low self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 他一点也不否认孩子们正处于各种痛苦之中，他们过得很艰难。

sentences.en: He doesn't deny at all that kids are in all sorts of distress, that they're having a really hard time.
sentences.zh: 但他认为这才是我们应该关注的地方。

sentences.en: But he thinks that's where our focus should be.
sentences.zh: 与其试图找出一种非常精确的生物标志物，不如看看这些孩子正在经历什么，并找出帮助他们的方法。

sentences.en: Rather than trying to figure out a very precise biomarker, let's look at the experience these kids are having and figure out how to help them.
sentences.zh: 因为你的伙伴，你知道，你的学校，你知道，这种失败时的羞耻感。

sentences.en: Because your mates, you know, your school, you know, this kind of sense of shame when you fail.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些对于长期的幸福感至关重要，不一定是生活上的成功，或者找份好工作之类的，

sentences.en: Those are the things I think are crucial in terms of the long term well-being of not necessarily success in life, but not getting a good job or anything,
sentences.zh: 仅仅是让自己内心感到快乐。

sentences.en: just being happy with it in yourself.
sentences.zh: 与其仅仅通过修复他们大脑的化学物质来试图“修复”他们，我们不如考虑如何让他们的环境更适合他们，

sentences.en: And instead of just trying to fix them by fixing the chemistry of their brain, we can think about how to make their environments more amenable to them,
sentences.zh: 以及如何帮助他们更好地应对环境中那些不适合他们的部分。

sentences.en: and also how to help them deal better with the parts of their environments that are not a good fit.
sentences.zh: 目标是增加技能和韧性，而不是减少多动症。

sentences.en: The goal is to add skills and resilience rather than to reduce ADHD.
sentences.zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Do you see what I mean?
sentences.zh: 所以改变的是目标。

sentences.en: So it's the goal that changes.
sentences.zh: 理论上，我完全理解改变孩子的环境而不是改变他们的大脑化学物质的理由。

sentences.en: I can totally see the case for changing a kid's environment rather than their brain chemistry in theory.
sentences.zh: 但在实践中，你知道，如果你很忙，你的孩子正在挣扎，而且手头有处方药可用，

sentences.en: But in practice, you know, if you're busy and your kid is struggling and there's a prescription available to you,
sentences.zh: 我也能理解为什么那是你会选择的方案。

sentences.en: I can also just see why that is the option that you'd want to choose.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜我很难想象，从实际操作层面来看，改变孩子的环境是什么样的？

sentences.en: And so I guess I'm having trouble envisioning, practically speaking, what does a change to a child's environment look like?
sentences.zh: 比如，这在某人的生活中会如何体现？

sentences.en: Like, how would that actually play out in somebody's life?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想这正是他和许多研究人员仍在努力解决的问题。

sentences.en: Well, I think that's something that he and a lot of researchers are still trying to work out.
sentences.zh: 我发现有一项研究非常感人。

sentences.en: There's this one study that I found really affecting.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是针对20世纪90年代那项最初的利他林研究中的同一批孩子进行的。

sentences.en: It's actually with the same kids who were in that original Ritalin study back in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 当他们进入青年期时，他们第一次能够对自己的生活和环境做出决定。

sentences.en: When they reached young adulthood, for the first time, they were able to make decisions about their lives and what their environment was.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人把自己放在了更适合自己的地方。

sentences.en: And a lot of them had put themselves in places where they fit better.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，他们的多动症问题正在消失。

sentences.en: And what they were finding was that their problems with ADHD were going away.
sentences.zh: 有一个年轻人进了电影学院，另一个开始理发，还有一个在修车。

sentences.en: So there was one young person who was in film school, another who had started cutting hair, another who was working on cars.
sentences.zh: 他们都描述说，当我做我感兴趣的事情时，这和我上高中的时候完全不同。

sentences.en: And they all described that when I'm doing something I'm interested in, it's so much different than it was when I was in high school.
sentences.zh: 这些是我真正喜欢、真正关心的东西。

sentences.en: This is stuff that I actually like, that I actually care about.
sentences.zh: 关于那项研究，我最喜欢的一点是，它也帮助我理解了埃德蒙·萨努加-巴克的经历。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I loved about that study was that it helped me understand Edmund Sanuga-Bark's experience as well.
sentences.zh: 因为他小时候在高中时，只是因为不适合，处在了对他大脑而言错误的地方。

sentences.en: Because he was a kid who, in high school, he was just in the wrong fit, in the wrong place for his particular brain.
sentences.zh: 他当时非常痛苦。

sentences.en: And he was miserable.
sentences.zh: 然后他进入了大学，这个非常学术的环境，突然间，他长时间深入思考问题的能力变得非常适用。

sentences.en: And then he gets to university, this very academic environment, where suddenly his ability to think deeply about things for a long period of time was perfectly well-suited.
sentences.zh: 突然间，他处于一个大脑能够适应的环境中。

sentences.en: And suddenly he's in an environment where his brain fits.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并不是说这些孩子在做和埃德蒙类似的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's not like these kids are doing something similar to what Edmund did, right?
sentences.zh: 比如寻找他们能够专注的环境。

sentences.en: Like finding environments where they could focus.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，保罗，埃德蒙对多动症的所有理解有多少是重新思考过的，这种重新思考有多少已经进入了主流视野？

sentences.en: So I wonder, Paul, how much of the way that Edmund is reconsidering all of his understanding about ADHD, how much of that reconsideration has broken through to the mainstream?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很难衡量。

sentences.en: I think it's kind of hard to measure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他所做的事情中复杂的一点是，他并不是真的在说，你知道，

sentences.en: I mean, one of the things that is complicated about what he's doing is that he's not really saying, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们应该停止使用兴奋剂药物或停止像现在这样频繁地进行诊断。

sentences.en: we should stop using stimulant medications or stop diagnosing as much as we are.
sentences.zh: 他谈论的是改变我们思考和谈论多动症的方式。

sentences.en: He is talking about changing the way that we think and talk about ADHD.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为这真的会产生影响。

sentences.en: But I do think that that really makes a difference.
sentences.zh: 我认为很多人开始相信，告诉孩子你身上有一种绝对的、本质的、固有的东西是有缺陷的，

sentences.en: And I think what a lot of people are coming to believe is that telling kids that there is this absolute essential inherent thing in you that is disordered,
sentences.zh: 你有这种缺陷，这实际上并不是给孩子传递有益的信息。

sentences.en: that you have this deficit, that that is not actually a helpful message to give to kids.
sentences.zh: 这往往会让他们觉得，自己被困在了大脑中某个坏掉的东西里。

sentences.en: That that can often make them feel like they are stuck in this thing that is just broken in their brain.
sentences.zh: 如果换个说法，你可以告诉孩子，你知道，现在你有这个问题，也许药物治疗是帮助解决它的正确方法。

sentences.en: And that if instead you can say to kids, you know, right now you have got this problem and maybe medication is the right thing to do to help with that.
sentences.zh: 但也许你的行为可以有所改变，或者环境可以有所改变，从而帮助你。

sentences.en: But maybe there's something that can change in your behavior or something that can change in the environment that can help you.

sentences.en: And next year, this symptom might not be there at all.

sentences.en: I mean, in some ways, I think it's harder for a family to not have this sort of clear, sharp definition of what the problem is.
